title: Heavy-Duty Trucks in 2027: Sales Are Falling, But Why Do They Hold Value?

scenes.text: The trucks that keep their value best, and the trucks most likely to last two hundred fifty thousand miles, are not the ones most people buy. They are heavy-duty pickups. And their sales are falling. In nine months, the three biggest heavy-duty lines lost more than twenty-two thousand sales. One heavy truck was just discontinued. Here is what the numbers say about heavy-duty trucks heading into twenty twenty-seven.
scenes.caption: HEAVY-DUTY TRUCKS IN 2027

scenes.text: A heavy-duty pickup is the truck behind the truck. It is the one with the dual rear wheels, the big diesel, and a bed that carries a ton. The model names are the two fifty, three fifty, and four fifty at Ford, and the two thousand five hundred and three thousand five hundred at Chevrolet, GMC and Ram. These are work trucks, and the people who buy them are often buying a tool for a business.
scenes.caption: THE TRUCK BEHIND THE TRUCK

scenes.text: For this video, we gathered five kinds of numbers. Sales, from the Pickup Truck Talk table for the first nine months of twenty twenty-six. Resale value, from iSeeCars. Longevity, from the iSeeCars study reported by Work Truck Online. Ford's production figures, from Ford Authority. And the medium-duty trucks, from Motor One and GM Authority. Every source is listed in the description, and every number is labeled.
scenes.caption: SALES, RESALE, LONGEVITY, PRODUCTION

scenes.text: There is a twist in every one of these trucks. One is growing while its rivals shrink. One is losing sales and still sits in the top group for lasting. One is the most expensive to lose value on, and the cheapest to keep. And one is a truck that you can no longer order. Stay with me, because the last twist is about the whole class, and what it means if you are thinking of buying a work truck.
scenes.caption: FIVE TWISTS ON HEAVY-DUTY TRUCKS

scenes.text: First, the whole class. Through nine months of twenty twenty-six, the three heavy-duty lines in the table, the Chevrolet Silverado HD, the GMC Sierra HD and the Ram HD, sold three hundred thirty-five thousand, two hundred sixteen. A year earlier, it was three hundred fifty-seven thousand, six hundred twenty-five. That is a fall of six point three percent, or twenty-two thousand, four hundred nine trucks.
scenes.caption: HD: 335,216 (-6.3%)

scenes.text: The third quarter was weaker still. Those three lines sold one hundred thirteen thousand, nine hundred eighty-nine in the quarter, compared with one hundred twenty-three thousand, six hundred seventy-one a year earlier, a fall of about seven point eight percent. Ford does not split its Super Duty sales in the sources we found, so it is not in these totals. Ford Authority reports only that Super Duty production in the quarter was one hundred ten thousand, two hundred seventy-five, up four point four percent.
scenes.caption: Q3: HD DOWN ~7.8%

scenes.text: Number one is the Ram heavy-duty, and it is the one growing. Through nine months, Ram sold one hundred twenty-three thousand, two hundred one heavy-duty trucks, up three point four percent from one hundred nineteen thousand, one hundred twenty-two. In a class that fell more than six percent, a gain of three point four is a clear lead.
scenes.caption: RAM HD: +3.4%

scenes.text: The twist is in the quarter. In the third quarter, the Ram HD sold forty-one thousand, one hundred seven, down six percent from forty-three thousand, seven hundred seventeen. So the growth was in the first half, and it slowed. Even so, the Ram is the only heavy-duty line in the table with a gain for the nine months. That is a very different picture from the Chevrolet and the GMC.
scenes.caption: Q3: RAM HD -6.0%

scenes.text: And it does very well on the iSeeCars lists. The Ram three thousand five hundred keeps seventy-nine point eight percent of its value after five years, the best of any heavy-duty truck, and the Ram two thousand five hundred keeps seventy-four point nine. In the longevity study, the Ram three thousand five hundred is first of all trucks, with a thirty-one point nine percent chance of reaching two hundred fifty thousand miles, nearly three times the truck average.
scenes.caption: RAM 3500: 79.8% RESALE, 31.9% LONGEVITY

scenes.text: Number two is the Chevrolet Silverado heavy-duty, and its numbers tell a harder story. Through nine months, Chevrolet sold one hundred thirty-three thousand, seven hundred sixty-nine, down thirteen percent from one hundred fifty-three thousand, seven hundred fifty. That is a loss of nearly twenty thousand trucks in a year, the biggest fall of any heavy-duty line in the table.
scenes.caption: SILVERADO HD: -13.0%

scenes.text: And the quarter did not rescue it. In the third quarter, the Silverado HD sold forty-four thousand, two hundred seventy-eight, down ten point one percent. The twist is that the light-duty Silverado, the same brand's everyday truck, grew six point five percent through nine months. So the same company is gaining with one truck and losing with the other. The work truck is the one in decline.
scenes.caption: Q3: -10.1%. LD SILVERADO: +6.5%.

scenes.text: On longevity, the Silverado two thousand five hundred HD is ninth, at fourteen point one percent, and the three thousand five hundred HD is twelfth at eleven point seven, barely above the truck average of eleven point one. In the earlier edition of the study, the two thousand five hundred HD was sixth, at forty-one point two percent. So the heavy-duty Silverado has slipped in the study, and it has slipped in sales.
scenes.caption: SILVERADO 2500HD: 14.1%. 3500HD: 11.7%.

scenes.text: Number three is the GMC Sierra heavy-duty. Through nine months, GMC sold seventy-eight thousand, two hundred forty-six, down seven point seven percent from eighty-four thousand, seven hundred fifty-three. In the third quarter, it sold twenty-eight thousand, six hundred four, down six point nine percent. A smaller fall than the Chevrolet, but a fall.
scenes.caption: SIERRA HD: -7.7%

scenes.text: Here is the twist. The Sierra three thousand five hundred HD is third in the longevity study, at twenty-six point two percent, about two and a half times the truck average. And the two thousand five hundred HD is fifth, at seventeen point two. So the GMC does much better than its Chevrolet twin on the longevity list, even though the two are built in the same way. A badge and a trim can matter more than the platform.
scenes.caption: SIERRA 3500HD: 26.2% (3RD)

scenes.text: Number four is the Ford Super Duty. We have no sales number for it, because the sources we found do not split it from the F-Series. What we have is the production figure, one hundred ten thousand, two hundred seventy-five in the third quarter, up four point four percent, according to Ford Authority. In a quarter when the three Detroit-badge heavy-duty trucks we could measure were falling, Ford was building more.
scenes.caption: SUPER DUTY: Q3 PRODUCTION 110,275 (+4.4%)

scenes.text: On resale, the Ford F-three-fifty keeps seventy-nine point six percent after five years, the F-four-fifty seventy-seven, and the F-two-fifty seventy-five point seven. Those are among the best numbers in the whole market. On longevity, the F-three-fifty is sixth at fifteen point one percent, the F-four-fifty seventh at fourteen point nine, and the F-two-fifty eleventh at thirteen point four. In the earlier edition, the F-three-fifty was first, at forty-nine point one.
scenes.caption: F-350: 79.6% RESALE

scenes.text: The twist is the contrast. The Super Duty is strong on resale and middling on longevity in the latest edition. The Ram is strong on both. And the Chevrolet is weaker on both. So the three big companies, all selling similar trucks to similar buyers, have different strengths. A buyer who looks only at the brand's reputation, and not at the numbers for the specific truck, might miss that.
scenes.caption: THREE COMPANIES, THREE PROFILES

scenes.text: Number five is the truck you can no longer order, the Chevrolet Silverado medium-duty. According to Motor One, Chevrolet is ending the Silverado four thousand five hundred, five thousand five hundred and six thousand five hundred HD, built with International Motors in Ohio. Production ended after the September thirtieth conclusion of the manufacturing agreement, and International is selling the plant. The sale was announced on March thirtieth.
scenes.caption: SILVERADO MEDIUM-DUTY: ENDED SEPT 30

scenes.text: The sales explain why. Chevrolet sold eight thousand, three hundred forty-one medium-duty trucks in twenty twenty-five, down nineteen point two percent. And in the first three months of twenty twenty-six, it sold one thousand, two hundred seventy-three, down thirty-seven point four percent. For comparison, Ford sold two thousand, three hundred thirty-one heavy trucks in the same period. So the truck was shrinking before it ended.
scenes.query: International Motors truck plant Springfield Ohio
scenes.caption: 2025: 8,341 (-19.2%). Q1 2026: 1,273 (-37.4%).

scenes.text: And here is the twist about what comes next. GM says it is evaluating future portfolio options for medium-duty, and will share more later. So there is no announced successor. And the article does not say what happens to current owners, including warranty or service. If you own one, or buy one from stock, ask the dealer directly, in writing, how parts and service will be handled after the production ended.
scenes.caption: NO ANNOUNCED SUCCESSOR

scenes.text: Let's put a half-ton and a heavy-duty truck side by side, using only the numbers we have. On resale, the Ford F-one-fifty keeps sixty-one point four percent after five years, and the F-three-fifty seventy-nine point six. The Ram one thousand five hundred keeps sixty-one point eight, and the Ram three thousand five hundred seventy-nine point eight. In both brands, the heavy-duty truck keeps about eighteen points more.
scenes.caption: RESALE: F-150 61.4% VS F-350 79.6%

scenes.text: On longevity, the picture is more mixed. In the latest edition, the Ram three thousand five hundred is first at thirty-one point nine percent, while the Ram one thousand five hundred is not in the top twelve. The Ford F-three-fifty is sixth at fifteen point one, and the F-one-fifty is not in the top twelve either. So for both companies, the heavy-duty truck is more likely to go the distance than its half-ton cousin.
scenes.caption: LONGEVITY: HD ABOVE HALF-TON

scenes.text: And on sales, the opposite holds. The Ford F-Series sold five hundred fifty-seven thousand through nine months, and the Silverado one thousand five hundred and two thousand five hundred together sold more than four hundred thousand. The half-tons dominate. So the market buys the truck that is easier to live with, and the truck that holds its value best is the one fewer people buy. That is a very old pattern in the truck business, and the numbers confirm it.
scenes.caption: HALF-TONS WIN ON SALES

scenes.text: So which should you buy? If you tow or haul heavy loads, every week, the heavy-duty truck is built for it, and the numbers on resale and longevity are on its side. If you use a truck mostly for commuting and family trips, with an occasional trailer, a half-ton is easier to drive, and often cheaper. The mistake is to buy the heavy-duty truck for the image, or to buy the half-ton and push it past its limits every weekend.
scenes.caption: BUY FOR THE JOB, NOT THE IMAGE

scenes.text: There is one more thing to consider, and it is about timing. A heavy-duty truck costs more to buy, and the numbers say that it loses less value. That means the money you pay at the start comes back more fully at the end. For a business, that matters, because the truck can be an asset on the balance sheet. For a private buyer, it may matter less, because the cash you tie up in the truck cannot be used elsewhere.
scenes.caption: MORE UPFRONT, MORE BACK LATER

scenes.text: Finally, a word about the numbers in this video. Most of them are estimates or reported figures from third parties, and they were collected in the fall of twenty twenty-six. Sales tables are reasonably precise, but resale and longevity numbers are statistical estimates. Use them to narrow the list, and then check the exact truck. The best information about a used truck is its service record and a careful inspection.
scenes.caption: ESTIMATES: USE THEM TO NARROW THE LIST

scenes.text: So what is the final twist? It is about why heavy-duty trucks are falling in sales, and the sources we found do not give a reason. We can offer what the numbers do say. The price of trucks has risen, the full-size average is sixty-seven thousand, four hundred forty-six dollars, and heavy-duty trucks are more expensive still. The market for work trucks may be more sensitive to price, and to the economy, than the market for family trucks. But that is an interpretation, not a finding.
scenes.caption: WHY ARE HD SALES FALLING?

scenes.text: What the numbers do show is that the heavy-duty trucks are a very different asset. They lose about twenty to twenty-five percent in five years, compared with thirty-eight to forty percent for a half-ton. Take an example of a truck that costs seventy thousand dollars new. At the Ram's or the Ford's rate, that is a loss of about fourteen thousand to seventeen thousand dollars. At the F-one-fifty's rate, it is about twenty-seven thousand. A work truck can be a better store of value than a family truck.
scenes.caption: HD LOSES ~20-25%. HALF-TON ~39%.

scenes.text: But a store of value is only useful if you can sell. In a market where the heavy-duty lines are shrinking, there may be fewer new trucks and fewer buyers, and that is something to watch. We do not have used price data in the sources we found. A careful buyer checks local prices for the exact truck, and compares the five-year picture to the cost of a lease or a rental, if the work is occasional.
scenes.caption: CHECK THE LOCAL USED MARKET

scenes.text: Before the checklist, let's read the main sales number in a calm way. The three heavy-duty lines sold three hundred thirty-five thousand, two hundred sixteen trucks in nine months, down six point three percent. That is a fall, but it is not a collapse. Hundreds of thousands of buyers still chose these trucks. Remember also that Ford is not in that total, because the sources do not split out the Super Duty. So do not read the table as proof that Ford is winning or losing. It tells you about three brands, and it says nothing more.
scenes.caption: A FALL IS NOT A COLLAPSE

scenes.text: Now, how to verify a heavy-duty truck before you buy it. Go to the door sticker. It lists the payload and the towing figure for that exact truck, and those depend on the engine, the axle and the cab. A brochure shows the best case, and the sticker shows the truck in front of you. Write down the two numbers, then compare them with the heaviest load you really carry. If the sticker figure is close to your load, you want a bigger margin, not a smaller one.
scenes.caption: READ THE DOOR STICKER, NOT THE BROCHURE

scenes.text: Let's also separate two numbers that people often blend together. Resale value is what the market thinks a truck will be worth. Longevity is the chance that a truck reaches two hundred fifty thousand miles. The Ram three thousand five hundred is strong on both, at seventy-nine point eight percent and thirty-one point nine. The Ford F-three-fifty is strong on resale at seventy-nine point six, but its longevity is fifteen point one. The Chevrolet three thousand five hundred HD is at eleven point seven, barely above the truck average of eleven point one. Different questions, different answers.
scenes.caption: RESALE AND LONGEVITY ARE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS

scenes.text: A word about the earlier edition of the study. The F-three-fifty was first at forty-nine point one percent, and in the latest edition it is sixth at fifteen point one. The Silverado two thousand five hundred HD was sixth at forty-one point two, and it is now ninth at fourteen point one. Those are big moves, and they tell you something useful. These are statistical estimates, and they change from one edition to the next. Use them to narrow your list, not to decide for you, and let the exact truck and its records have the final word.
scenes.caption: STUDIES CHANGE FROM EDITION TO EDITION

scenes.text: If you are considering the Silverado medium-duty, or any truck that has just ended, be careful and practical. The sources do not say how warranty or service will be handled after production ended, so do not assume. Ask the dealer to answer in writing, and ask how parts will be supplied. Ask whether the price reflects the fact that there is no announced successor. A truck can still be a good tool when the line is gone, but you should be paying for that situation, and you should know about it before you sign.
scenes.caption: ASK FOR PARTS AND SERVICE IN WRITING

scenes.text: Who should buy a heavy-duty truck, and who should wait? It suits the person who tows or hauls heavy loads every week, or a business that needs a tool and values what the truck is worth later. It may not suit a commuter with an occasional trailer, because a half-ton is easier to drive and costs less to buy. And it is a reason to wait if you cannot find local used prices for the exact truck, because a store of value only helps when there are buyers on the other side.
scenes.caption: WHO IT SUITS, AND WHO SHOULD WAIT

scenes.text: Last, the common mistakes. Buying a heavy-duty truck for the image. Trusting a brand's reputation instead of the numbers for the specific model. Comparing one company's top trim with another company's base trim. And accepting the first quote. Get the same configuration quoted by the Ford, Ram and Chevrolet dealers on the same day, in writing, with the full price. In a market where Ram is growing and Chevrolet is falling, the offers may not be equal, and the only way to find out is to ask.
scenes.caption: COMPARE THE SAME TRUCK ON THE SAME DAY

scenes.text: A short routine before you visit a dealer. Decide how heavy your real load is, and write it down. Look up the door sticker figures for the trucks on your list. Ask each brand for the same configuration, in writing, with the full price. Then compare the five-year resale figures for those exact models, remembering that Ram and Ford are strong there, and the half-ton keeps much less. Finally, ask whether the model is still being built. If every answer is clear, you are choosing with your eyes open, which is all any set of numbers can really do for you.
scenes.caption: A SHORT ROUTINE BEFORE THE DEALER

scenes.text: So what should you check before you buy a heavy-duty truck in twenty twenty-seven? First, whether you really need one, because a half-ton can do a lot. Second, the exact configuration, the engine, the axle, the payload and the towing figure on the door sticker. Third, the five-year resale value for that model. And fourth, whether the model is still being built, because the Silverado medium-duty shows that it can end.
scenes.caption: CHECK 1, 2, 3 AND 4
scenes.chapter: What to check before you buy in 2027

scenes.text: We put all of this into a checklist, the Twenty Twenty-Seven Truck Buyer's Guide. It covers the numbers to check, the questions to ask a dealer, and the warning signs we walked through. The link is in the description and in the pinned comment. If you want to know which engines to avoid in a used truck, subscribe, because that is coming soon. Thanks for watching.
